narrator.how: quiet, plain and close, an Irish man's low voice reading a short book aloud by the fire: only what is seen, no pity in the voice, the weight left in the pauses

bill.how: a tired working man near forty, soft-spoken and few-worded, Irish; never raises his voice; the truth he says quietly, and short

eileen.how: a brisk Irish housewife, quick and practical, counting as she talks; warm to her own, sharp and dry about others; when it hurts — faster, not louder

sara.how: a girl of seventeen, Irish, hoarse from the cold; a whisper in one breath; lies quickly and evenly with a smile in the voice; asks about her boy flatly, almost as a challenge

mother.how: the Mother Superior: warm, unhurried, very polite, never raising her voice; every kindness lands as an obligation; questions instead of answers

kehoe.how: an older Irish woman behind a café counter: grumbling and kind, her important things in a whisper, her eyes on who is listening

sheila.how: a girl of twelve who sings in the convent choir: bright, quick, full of herself; gloating or in tears, nothing in between

kathleen.how: a girl of fourteen, the eldest: sulky and cross, short words; hurt she does not show except by banging things

loretta.how: a small girl, the youngest: earnest and curious, says what she sees

grace.how: a girl of eight with a mouthful of raisins: matter-of-fact, out of breath from running

worker.how: a coal-yard hand, Irish, gravelly and joking, grumbling about money

sister.how: a nun of the convent: smiling, smooth and cool, every word in its place

young.how: a young country nun at the grille at night: low and quick, afraid of being heard, sorry and firm

wilson.how: an old Protestant widow, remembered: calm, dry, settling a thing once and for all

tenant.how: a countryman at a gate: easy, chatty, saying everything in the same tone as the weather

oldman.how: a very old man met in the fog: slow and kind, a little odd

dougherty.how: a nosy neighbour on the street: loud, shocked, saying it to your face

postman.how: the postman in the café: friendly, offhand, in a hurry

nephew.how: Mrs Kehoe's young nephew: awkward, mumbling
